new A-R5.5 for the rules-layer per-cell check; R-5 gained the explicit rejection rule; A-R2.1 and
R-2 gained a server-rendered grid contract with `data-row`/`data-col` and an exact count; R-7
gained 405 and 413 plus precise field typing; A-R3.2/A-R3.3/A-R3.4 gained seeds `1..200`, seeds
`1..20` and a 200-attempt budget with a degenerate-source test; A-R9.1/A-R9.4 name the two test
files, a minimum count and the required cases. `RUN/notes/research.md` decision 8 was revised to
record the server-rendered grid and why the client-built alternative was rejected. Requirement IDs
R-1…R-10 and all other acceptance IDs were preserved.
class:
non-trivial — five acceptance lines were materially rewritten and two API boundaries added;
a weaker test would have passed several of the originals.
found:
Six material defects, all confirmed by walking the spec against itself.
1. **A-R5.1 could not happen.** It required firing at all 100 cells, but R-6.3 refuses any shot
   after `gameOver` with 409, so the walk is stopped by its own spec before the 100th cell. It also
   promised to assert per-cell outcomes "against the known fleet" at the HTTP layer, which is
   impossible without serializing the fleet — the very thing R-3.5 forbids.
2. **A-R2.1 was unobservable.** It required counting 100 cells, but the page plan built the grid in
   client script; no dependency-free test can see that. A weaker stand-in (matching `<title>` only)
   would have passed it.
3. **R-7 missed two boundaries its own NFR table relied on:** no status for a body over the 1 MB
   cap the capacity row names, and none for a known path with the wrong method — both reachable
   requests with no defined outcome.
4. **A-R3.4 was unbounded.** "Bounded attempt budget" had no number, so the degenerate-random test
   could hang; and A-R3.2/A-R3.3 said "varied seeds" and "different sequences" without naming any.
5. **A-R9.1/A-R9.4 were untestable as written:** "covered by at least one named test" names no
   files, no cases and no count.
6. **A-R5 was missing the rules-layer contract** behind the 409: nothing said the rules module
   rejects a repeat or post-game shot rather than silently ignoring it.
label: non-trivial

changed:
`docs/shiploop/spec.md` (commit `ebb1d7254927`): R-7 declares ids opaque and unvalidated,
so an unknown string id is 404 and only a missing/non-string/empty `game` is 400; R-2 requires the
status region to announce the win in words with New Game still available, with new A-R2.6 to
confirm it; R-10 states that a game's state changes inside the synchronous call after the body is
parsed, with new A-R10.5 testing the concurrent double shot via `Promise.all`; A-R10.2 is now an
HTTP test over two ids; A-R9.1's floor rises to 14 tests and A-R9.4 lists both new cases. No
requirement ID or previously existing acceptance ID was removed or renumbered.
class:
non-trivial — three contract clauses were added or tightened and one check moved from a
manual browser observation to an automated test.
found:
Three material gaps survived pass 1.
1. **R-7 had no status for a string-but-invalid id.** It defined 400 for a "well-formed id the
   server does not know" as 404 and 400 for a "missing, wrong-type or empty `game`", leaving
   `"abc"` — a non-empty string that is not a UUID — between the two rules. Two implementations
   would answer differently, and a client could be told `400` for a game it legitimately holds if
   id validation were ever narrowed.
2. **R-2 never promised a win state.** It disabled the grid after `gameOver` and announced each
   shot, but a player who sank the last ship was told nothing about having won. The UI guidance
   requires a success state, and R-2 as written made one optional. A weaker check (grid disabled)
   would have passed it.
3. **R-10 left simultaneous change unaddressed** even though the state/data assessment asks how it
   resolves. Two clients cannot share a game, but two in-flight shots at one cell can both read
   "not yet fired" if the mutation ever acquires an `await`; the spec neither fixed the interleaving
   point nor tested it. A second, smaller defect sat beside it: A-R10.2 confirmed per-game isolation
   with two browser tabs when two ids over HTTP observe the same property more cheaply and without
   a human.
label: non-trivial

changed:
`docs/shiploop/spec.md` (commit `02c1aac90e26`): R-1 accepts only an integer in `1..65535`

match exactly and that `/api/fire/` is therefore 404; A-R7.1's table gains `/api/fire/`,

class:
non-trivial — two public-contract boundaries were defined where they had been left to the
implementer.
found:
Two boundary rules were still open, both reachable by an ordinary client, plus two
confirmations the previous handoff asked for.
1. **R-1's port rule was undefined for empty and zero values.** "`Number(process.env.PORT)` when
   that is a valid port number, otherwise 3000" makes `PORT=""` parse to `0`, and `0` is a valid
   request for an ephemeral port — so an empty environment value would silently bind a random port
   instead of 3000, while the acceptance line only tested `PORT=abc`.
2. **R-7 left trailing-slash paths undefined.** A known path with a wrong method is 405 and an
   unknown path is 404, but `/api/fire/` and `/api` are neither, so the two rules do not decide
   them.
3. **Confirmed, no defect:** A-R2.1's exact pair count is satisfiable by a plain shell plus string
   injection — probed, 100 pair matches and ten-per-row counts with no template engine

4. **Confirmed, no defect:** A-R2.1's per-row count is unaffected by any other markup, because the

changed:

stripped**, with `/api/fire/` and `/api` as the unknown near-misses, and R-7's `404` clause says

class:
non-trivial — one public routing rule was left undefined by the previous pass, and two
checkable requirements had no acceptance line.
found:
Four defects, three of them created by the previous pass's own wording.
1. **R-7's exact-path rule left the query string undecided.** Pass 3 said paths "match exactly"
   and that `/api/fire/` is therefore `404`. Neither clause covered `/api/new?x=1`: it is not
   exactly `/api/new`, so an exact-match reader answers `404`, but it is also plainly the known
   path with a query bolted on, so a reader who strips the query answers `200`. A browser or a
   probe appending a cache-buster would have hit an undefined contract.
2. **R-7 still called the unknown-id case "a well-formed id".** Pass 2 had decided ids are opaque
   and never validated for format; the earlier phrase survived and invited an implementer to
   validate UUID shape before the lookup — exactly the choice pass 2 removed.
3. **The accessibility NFR row claimed a criterion no acceptance line stated.** It listed
   "results not conveyed by colour alone" as observable in A-R2.5, but A-R2.5 required only
   keyboard operation, accessible names and a status announcement. Colour-only marking — the
   most common failure of a grid game — would have passed.
4. **R-2's "shows how many ships remain" had no acceptance line.** A-R2.2 confirmed the fired cell
   changed colour/state; a page that never displayed a count would have passed the whole suite.

changed:
`docs/shiploop/spec.md`: A-R10.2 now names its three assertions (B accepts an unfired
cell with `200`/`gameOver: false` after A reaches `gameOver`; B's earlier `(0,0)` shot still

class:
non-trivial — one acceptance line was replaced by a verifiable predicate and one NFR row's
claimed criterion was given its line.
found:
1. **A-R10.2 named no observable predicate.** It required a test that "asserts each response is
   consistent with its own game" — no assertion a reader could replay, and no way to tell a real
   independence check from a vacuous one. It also asked the test to fire the same coordinates at
   both games, which proves nothing on its own because the two fleets differ. A verifiable form
   exists that needs no fleet knowledge: fire once at B, drive A to `gameOver`, then check B still
   accepts an unfired cell and still refuses its first cell.
2. **The performance NFR row claimed "never reloads the document" with no acceptance line behind
   it.** A-R2.2 covered one request per shot but not the reload, so a page that navigated on each
   shot — losing its game id — would have satisfied every line while failing the row.
3. **Cleared, no defect:** A-R6.2's 16th/17th ship-cell states hold for every fleet. After the
   16th ship cell exactly one ship cell is unfired, which can leave exactly one ship unsunk, so
   `shipsRemaining` is 1 and never 2; the 17th completes it. Recomputation in
   `CHILD/reviews/checks.md` §3.
4. **Cleared, no defect:** R-10's "pending marker" is bounded by "never guesses a result
   optimistically", and A-R2.4 requires a failed request to show an error and re-enable the grid,
   so the phrase cannot be read as permission for a guessed result.
5. **Cleared, no defect:** every status the prose names (400, 404, 405, 409, 413) has a row in

changed:

class:
non-trivial — one acceptance line was unsatisfiable as written and was replaced with a
measured, runnable check.
found:
1. **A-R9.1 required an observation `node --test` does not produce.** It demanded that both test

   prints test-case names only — `✔ alpha one`, `✔ alpha two`, `✔ beta one` — with no file paths,
   so the line could never be confirmed as written. It was the exact failure mode the pass-5
   handoff named: a check whose named confirmer cannot observe its subject.
2. **Cleared, no defect: the S1–S5 mapping.** S1 → R-1/R-9 (server, no dependencies), S2 → R-1

3. **Cleared, no defect: every remaining acceptance line's confirmer can see its subject.** The

evidence record was inaccurate.
found:
1. **A-R3.4 rested on a timeout that does not exist.** It required the degenerate-source test to
   throw "within the test's normal timeout". `node:test`'s per-test timeout defaults to `Infinity`,
   so no timeout would ever bound a hanging placement: the suite would stall rather than fail, and
   the line's own escape clause ("rather than … hanging") was unenforced. Measured: an explicit
   `{ timeout: 100 }` cancels a 1000 ms case, reports it under "failing tests" and makes
   `node --test` exit 1 (`RUN/scratch/node-test-timeout-probe.txt`).
2. **The "Evidence limits" bullet was stale.** It said the only measurements were the environment
   probes and the baseline run, but the spec's own checks now depend on three further host probes

class:

covered, including the request's headline no-dependency constraint.
found:
The unenforced-mechanism class is closed — the scan returns no such wording, and all three
open gaps name an owner and a stage. What remained was the class pass 4 named and this review then
swept systematically: a behaviour stated in a requirement's prose with no acceptance line. A

2. **R-2's "`data-row="0" data-col="0"` is the top-left cell" had no line.** A-R2.1 counted cells

class:
non-trivial — two accepted documents stated incompatible port rules, and the spec now
records which one binds.
found:
1. **R-1 and research decision 10 state different port rules.** Decision 10 says
   `Number(process.env.PORT) || 3000`, under which `-1`, `70000` and `1.5` are all accepted as
   ports; R-1 accepts only an integer in `1..65535` and falls back to 3000, which A-R1.3 checks
   with `70000`. The spec is the accepted artifact and pass 3 tightened it deliberately, but the
   research note is a planning input cited in the spec's own basis, and a planner reading decision
   10 alone would implement a rule that fails A-R1.3. A conflict between accepted documents is
   the one thing the packet says to surface rather than silently resolve.
2. **Cleared, no defect: decisions 1–9 all agree with the requirements that carry them.** The
   table is in `CHILD/reviews/checks.md` §3. Decision 5 lists only 400/404/409 but does not claim
   completeness, so R-7's 405 and 413 extend it rather than contradict it; decision 7's
   `README.md`/`.gitignore` are extra to the spec, not contrary to it.
3. **Cleared, no defect: the acceptance lines do not force shared mutable state in one test
   file.** Every HTTP case creates its own game inside its own case, and the rules cases take an
   injected source; no case needs to observe another's game object.
4. **Not a defect: the document's size.** Ten requirements and 39 lines for a five-file product is
   more than the minimum, but each line traces to a request sentence or a stated behaviour, and

class:
non-trivial — an accessibility expectation the spec claims to accept had no line, and the
obvious way to fail it is the most common keyboard-UI defect.

1. **A-R2.5 did not require a visible focus indicator, which the environment file lists as an
   accessibility expectation for this page.** A page styling `button:focus { outline: none }`
   would have satisfied every acceptance line while leaving a keyboard user unable to see which
   cell they were on — the single most common way a keyboard-operable grid becomes unusable. The
   NFR accessibility row had quietly dropped the criterion while still claiming to accept the
   environment's expectations.
2. **Cleared, no defect: the rest of the knowledge walk agrees with the spec.** The table is in
   `CHILD/reviews/checks.md` §3: commands, built-ins, module system, error contract, RNG
   injection, interaction and state ownership all map to requirements; discovery's two open
   questions (should `/api/new` carry dimensions; does the page need a "New game" control) are

   each test name with its outcome") matches the pass-6 measurement and makes no file-naming claim.

   once, test it against `Number.isInteger` and the range, then listen on the chosen port; no line
   requires binding first and validating afterwards.

class:
non-trivial — the pass changed fixture behaviour on a failure path, extended a required
boundary case, and corrected a knowledge-home claim that the reviewed file itself had just
falsified. Every exit clause was checked on its own against the artifacts after the last change:
the suite runs green on two runs, the default suite still reports 26, the catalog's eight fields
match the cases, and each system-level criterion still has a system case or a planned check with its
due stage.
found:
1. **The fixture teardown could hand a live listener to the next case.** `stopChild` sent `SIGTERM`
   and returned without waiting; a child that ignored it kept its port, and `freePort()` — which
   asks the OS for *any* free port and closes it — could then hand that same port to the next case,
   whose failure would read as a product fault ("no startup line within 5 s") rather than a fixture
   leak. Material: it is the suite's isolation contract, not a cosmetic improvement.
2. **A child that exited at once was reported as a timeout.** `startServer` polled only for the
   startup line, so a child killed by a stolen port (`EADDRINUSE`, `server.js:195-197`) failed after
   the full 5 s with `no startup line within 5 s` — a message that names the wrong cause and gives
   no retry for the probe-to-spawn race the component fixture rule already anticipates.
3. **`SYS_PORT_RESOLUTION` covered five of the seven documented fallbacks.** `README.md`'s Run-it
   section says any `PORT` that is not an integer in `1..65535` falls back to 3000; the case ran
   unset, empty, `abc`, `0` and `70000`, so a negative value and a fractional one — the two a person
   is most likely to type — were unobserved at process level, and `TC_PORT_DEFAULTS` (the terminal
   procedure) does not name them either. Material: required boundary coverage, not new scope.
4. **The recorded figures drifted the moment the fixture changed** — `environment.md`'s command
   cost ("six processes in turn"), §6's Setup-and-isolation and Cost lines ("about ten child
   starts"), the plan's `SYS_PORT_RESOLUTION` variant list and the catalog note's row, boundary
   paragraph and measured line all described the pre-edit suite. This is exactly the class commit
   `021c581` names: after one edit, the same statement is stale everywhere else in the file.

   gained the new file.** Line 436 said "no case asserts the address … not observable over HTTP from
   here", while `spec.md`'s R-1 status (corrected by the reviewed stage) says `SYS_LOOPBACK` now
   asserts it. The real-boundary table listed no `SYS_*` row, and the shape sentence, file table,
   module table and boundary table named the browser suite as the only opt-in suite. Material: the
   knowledge home's own inventory and a falsified observability claim.
6. Out of scope, recorded for product acceptance: `README.md:175` describes the decisions as
   `AD-1…AD-17` while `architecture.md` holds `AD-1…AD-19`. `README.md` is outside this review's
   scope (result + `docs/shiploop`), so it was not edited.

found:
1. **A wait's failure message was built before the wait, so it reported a snapshot of nothing.**
   `until(check, ms, message)` took a string, and every caller quoting a child's streams built it
   with a template literal at call time. A control run proved the cost: with `PORT` parsed by
   `Number.parseInt` (a mutation of `server.js`'s `portFrom`, reverted immediately), `PORT=1.5`
   resolves to port 1 and the child exits 1 with an `EACCES` stack — yet the pass-1 suite spent
   5446 ms and reported `PORT fractional neither started nor refused: {"stdout":"","stderr":""}`,
   twice (`improve-sta-mutant-port.txt`, `improve-sta-mutant-port-old-wait.txt`). A failure that
   names the wrong evidence is the same class as the two findings pass 1 fixed, and it made the
   suite's own red runs unreadable. Material.

   `startServer` to fail at once when a child exits; the `PORT` case kept its own inline poll, so a

   that names neither the exit nor the streams — the only path where "the value the product
   mishandles" was not named. Material: same contract, one helper behind.
